title: GPUs All Grown-Up: Fully Device-Driven SpMV Using GPU Work Graphs
problem: Sparse matrix-vector multiplication (SpMV) on GPUs requires expensive host-side preprocessing to select per-row algorithms based on non-zero distribution, forcing costly CPU-GPU round-trips and limiting cache locality. This preprocessing adds latency that is particularly problematic for iterative solvers with repeated SpMV calls.
motivation: SpMV is a fundamental kernel in HPC and graph analytics, and its irregular sparsity patterns make static per-row algorithm selection at compile time impossible, yet existing GPU approaches pay high overhead for dynamic selection through host involvement.
method: The paper leverages GPU Work Graphs, a novel GPU programming model originally designed for graphics, to implement fully device-driven SpMV self-scheduling. Work Graphs enable fine-grained dataflow execution of individual workgroups using emerging GPU hardware and firmware support (AMD GPUs with rocSPARSE stack). Preprocessing is fused with per-row computation: as soon as preprocessing generates sufficient work metadata, workgroups of specialized per-row SpMV kernels are self-scheduled and dispatched on-device without host interaction. This interleaving improves L1/L2 cache locality and eliminates CPU-GPU synchronization entirely. The approach uses a fixed 25 MiB device-side supporting data structure independent of matrix size, contrasting with scaling structures in rocSPARSE LRB.
key_novelty: Applying GPU Work Graphs—a hardware/firmware-level on-device self-scheduling mechanism—to SpMV to fuse preprocessing and per-row computation on the GPU, eliminating host interaction and improving cache locality.
contributions: First application of GPU Work Graphs to sparse linear algebra (SpMV), enabling fully device-driven preprocessing and execution.
Novel Work Graphs SpMV kernels that self-schedule per-row algorithms based on dynamically determined non-zero structure.
Up to 7.19x speedup (mean 3.35x) over rocSPARSE LRB for single SpMV across 59 sparse matrices.
75% reduction in code complexity and a fixed 25 MiB memory footprint independent of matrix size.

metrics.speedup: up to 7.19x (mean 3.35x, SD 1.89) over rocSPARSE LRB for single SpMV; beats rocSPARSE CSR-Adaptive for up to 92 consecutive SpMV calls
metrics.other: 75% reduction in code complexity; fixed 25 MiB data structure vs. matrix-size-scaling rocSPARSE LRB structures

limitations: Evaluation is limited to AMD GPUs supporting Work Graphs (rocSPARSE/ROCm ecosystem); portability to NVIDIA CUDA and generalization to SpMM or other sparse kernels is not demonstrated.
primary_theme: device-driven GPU self-scheduling for sparse matrix-vector multiplication
